defects.title: Placeholder-less f-string in rewrite.py (ruff F541) turns the CI 'Static check with Ruff' step red

browser-use__browser-use@aab7b3b.pr_summary: Switches the library from playwright to patchright (an undetected Playwright fork): every playwright.async_api / playwright._impl._errors import under browser_use/ (plus two tests and a docs snippet) is repointed to patchright, and patchright>=1.51.0 is added to dependencies alongside playwright. The builtin launch now passes channel='chrome'; BrowserContextConfig.user_agent defaults to None and is only passed when set; new contexts only get viewport/no_viewport=False in headless mode (the old unconditional no_viewport=True is gone), and bypass_csp/ignore_https_errors are passed only when disable_security is on. The anti-detection init script is cut down to the permissions.query patch (webdriver/languages/plugins/window.chrome overrides and the attachShadow open-mode override are removed). Browser.new_context now defaults to self.config.new_context_config, browser_binary_path uses validation_alias, and Agent.__init__ copies the browser-level disable_security onto the browser's new_context_config.

defects.title: Hard-coded channel='chrome' makes the default launch require a system Google Chrome - agents fail to start after the documented `playwright install chromium`
defects.statement: _setup_builtin_browser - the path for every Browser()/Agent() without cdp_url, wss_url or browser_binary_path - now always calls browser_class.launch(..., channel='chrome', ...). With the default browser_class 'chromium' this selects the branded Google Chrome stable install instead of the Playwright-managed Chromium. On machines without Chrome (Linux servers, Docker, CI, anyone who followed the README's `playwright install chromium`) launch raises "Chromium distribution 'chrome' is not found", _setup_browser re-raises, and the agent cannot start.
defects.evidence: head/browser_use/browser/browser.py:281-288 `browser = await browser_class.launch(headless=self.config.headless, channel='chrome', args=args[self.config.browser_class], ...)`; :91 `browser_class: Literal['chromium', 'firefox', 'webkit'] = 'chromium'`; :302-305 route every config without browser_binary_path to `_setup_builtin_browser`. head/README.md:31-34 `Install Playwright: playwright install chromium` (no Chrome install). Playwright's 'chrome' channel resolves to the system Chrome path and errors when it is absent.
defects.notes: Counts if the comment says the unconditional channel='chrome' requires Google Chrome (not the Playwright/bundled Chromium the README installs), so the default launch fails where Chrome is not installed. A comment only about firefox/webkit counts for D3, not here; a generic 'patchright may behave differently' remark does not count.

defects.title: Headful (default) contexts no longer pass no_viewport=True, so a fixed 1280x720 emulated viewport sits inside the screen-sized window
defects.statement: Base created every new context with no_viewport=True, so the page viewport tracked the real window (launched with --window-size=<screen resolution> in headful mode). Head sets viewport kwargs only when browser.config.headless is true; in headful mode (the default, headless=False) neither viewport nor no_viewport is passed and Playwright falls back to its default emulated 1280x720 viewport. Pages render and are inspected at 1280x720 inside a full-screen window: less content is visible to the DOM extractor and screenshots, responsive layouts change, and innerWidth/outerWidth disagree (itself a bot signal for an anti-detection PR).
defects.evidence: head/browser_use/browser/context.py:413-416 `kwargs = {}` / `if self.browser.config.headless:` / `kwargs['viewport'] = self.config.browser_window_size` / `kwargs['no_viewport'] = False`; :420-421 `context = await browser.new_context(**kwargs, ...)` - nothing viewport-related in the headful branch. Base: `context = await browser.new_context(no_viewport=True, ...)`. head/browser.py:97 `headless: bool = False`; :244-255 headful uses `get_screen_resolution()` for `--window-size`. Playwright new_context defaults to a 1280x720 viewport unless no_viewport=True.
defects.notes: Must tie the regression to headful mode: no no_viewport/viewport is passed when headless=False, so the default fixed viewport is used / the viewport no longer matches the window. Near-miss that must NOT count on its own: 'the no_viewport config field is ignored' (it was ignored in base too) or remarks about the headless viewport now using browser_window_size.

defects.title: channel='chrome' is also passed to the firefox/webkit launchers, which reject it - browser_class 'firefox'/'webkit' can no longer launch
defects.statement: browser_class still accepts 'firefox' and 'webkit' and the args dict just above still carries per-engine arguments for them, but the same launch call now passes channel='chrome' to whichever BrowserType was selected. Playwright resolves the channel to the Chrome executable, whose browserName is chromium, and throws `Unsupported firefox channel "chrome"` (likewise for webkit), so those supported configurations fail to launch on every machine, whether or not Chrome is installed.
defects.evidence: head/browser_use/browser/browser.py:91 `browser_class: Literal['chromium', 'firefox', 'webkit'] = 'chromium'`; :264 `browser_class = getattr(playwright, self.config.browser_class)`; :265-279 `args = {'chromium': ..., 'firefox': [... '-no-remote' ...], 'webkit': [... '--no-startup-window' ...]}`; :281-283 `browser_class.launch(headless=..., channel='chrome', args=args[self.config.browser_class], ...)`. Playwright server browserType: `const registryExecutable = registry.findExecutable(options.channel || this._name); if (!registryExecutable || registryExecutable.browserName !== this._name) throw new Error(`Unsupported ${this._name} channel "${options.channel}"`)`.
defects.notes: Must say the hard-coded channel='chrome' is passed to (or invalid for) the firefox/webkit browser_class and breaks their launch. A comment only about Chrome needing to be installed counts for D1, not here.

defects.title: Agent.__init__ unconditionally overwrites new_context_config.disable_security with the browser-level flag, clobbering an explicit context setting and mutating the caller's Browser
defects.statement: Agent now assigns self.browser.config.new_context_config.disable_security = self.browser.config.disable_security on every construction. A caller who set only the context-level flag (BrowserConfig default disable_security=False, new_context_config=BrowserContextConfig(disable_security=True)) - honoured by base - has it silently reset to False, so ignore_https_errors/bypass_csp are dropped and e.g. self-signed intranet sites fail; conversely BrowserConfig(disable_security=True) with an explicit context-level False now gets CSP bypass and certificate errors ignored. The write also mutates an injected, possibly shared Browser, so later contexts created from it (including Browser.new_context()) depend on whether an Agent was constructed first.
defects.evidence: head/browser_use/agent/service.py:260-261 `self.browser = browser or Browser()` / `self.browser.config.new_context_config.disable_security = self.browser.config.disable_security`; head/browser.py:98 `disable_security: bool = False`; head/context.py:144 context-level `disable_security: bool = False`; :423 `**({'bypass_csp': True, 'ignore_https_errors': True} if self.config.disable_security else {})`. Base _create_context used `bypass_csp=self.config.disable_security` with the context config untouched by Agent.
defects.notes: Must say the Agent line overrides/clobbers an explicitly set context-level disable_security (either direction) or mutates the injected/shared Browser config. A comment merely restating the line, praising the sync, or only asking for the flag to also flow through Browser.new_context() (see C6 exclusion) does not count.

defects.title: Dropping the attachShadow open-mode override hides elements inside closed shadow roots from the DOM extractor
defects.statement: The base init script wrapped Element.prototype.attachShadow to force mode 'open', which is what let buildDomTree.js descend into shadow trees via node.shadowRoot. The PR deletes that block together with the stealth overrides. For pages that create closed shadow roots, node.shadowRoot is now null, buildDomTree skips the subtree, and the agent can no longer see or interact with those controls - a functional capability loss unrelated to detection evasion.
defects.evidence: Base context.py:472-477 `const originalAttachShadow = Element.prototype.attachShadow; Element.prototype.attachShadow = function attachShadow(options) { return originalAttachShadow.call(this, { ...options, mode: "open" }); };` - removed; head context.py:447-457 keeps only the permissions.query patch. head/browser_use/dom/buildDomTree.js:977-979 `if (node.shadowRoot) { nodeData.shadowRoot = true; for (const child of node.shadowRoot.childNodes) {` - Element.shadowRoot is null for closed roots.
defects.notes: Must mention the removed attachShadow/force-open override and its effect on closed shadow DOM extraction/interaction. Remarks only about losing webdriver/plugins/languages/window.chrome spoofing do not count (deliberately delegated to patchright).

excluded.reason: Not introduced/worsened: in base, Browser.new_context() passed the BrowserConfig itself as the context config and _create_context then read self.config.user_agent (base context.py:418), which BrowserConfig lacks - that path crashed. In head it works and, like the base Agent path, applies the context-level new_context_config.disable_security; the browser-level flag never reached contexts in base either. Consistency wish, not a regression.
Documentation wording nit (surrounding docs text still says 'Playwright'); patchright is API-compatible and the snippet is correct. Not a code defect.

vllm-project__vllm@134705b.pr_summary: Extends vllm/logger.py so info_once/warning_once accept lazy %-style positional args (*args: Hashable) and forward them through the lru_cache'd _print_info_once/_print_warning_once helpers to logger.info/warning; the dedupe key becomes (logger, msg, *args). Call sites in config.py, punica_selector, custom_op, xgrammar_decoding, awq_marlin, weight_utils, chameleon/olmoe/qwen2_moe/qwen3_moe and multimodal profiling/registry are converted from f-strings to a format string plus args, with `# noqa: E501` on the long literals. A few docstring trailing spaces are removed.

defects.title: Multimodal profiling passes a dict to the lru_cache'd warning_once, raising TypeError: unhashable type 'dict' and aborting V0 profiling/engine startup instead of warning
defects.statement: _print_warning_once is decorated with functools.lru_cache, which hashes every positional argument to build its cache key. Both converted warnings in MultiModalProfiler (encoder: get_encoder_dummy_data; decoder: get_decoder_dummy_data) pass self._get_mm_num_tokens(mm_inputs), which returns a dict {modality: num_tokens}. When the warning condition holds (V0, total_len > seq_len), the call raises TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict' before anything is logged, so dummy-data construction, memory profiling and engine start-up abort where base only printed a warning. Reachable with normal configs: encoder-decoder models such as Llama-3.2-Vision (mllama) run on V0, the enc-dec profile_run does not shrink max_num_seqs, and seq_len = max_num_batched_tokens // max_num_seqs is far below the thousands of encoder image tokens; decoder-only multimodal models hit the decoder branch on V0 when max_num_batched_tokens < max_mm_tokens.
defects.evidence: head/vllm/multimodal/profiling.py:185-194 `def _get_mm_num_tokens(...) -> Mapping[str, int]: ... return { modality: sum(...) for modality, placeholders in placeholders_by_modality.items() }`; :215-225 `elif total_len > seq_len and not envs.VLLM_USE_V1: logger.warning_once("...%d...%d...%s...", seq_len, total_len, self._get_mm_num_tokens(mm_inputs),)`; same at :240-250. head/vllm/logger.py:61-64 `@lru_cache def _print_warning_once(logger: Logger, msg: str, *args: Hashable) -> None: logger.warning(msg, *args, stacklevel=2)`; init_logger binds warning_once = MethodType(_print_warning_once, logger) (logger.py:132-139), so the dict goes into the lru_cache key -> hash(dict) -> TypeError. Callers: worker/enc_dec_model_runner.py:305-318 and worker/model_runner.py:1310-1318 profile_run -> input_registry.dummy_data_for_profiling -> MultiModalRegistry.get_encoder/decoder_dummy_data. An AST scan of every multi-arg info_once/warning_once call in head finds no other unhashable argument.
defects.notes: Must identify that an unhashable value (the dict from _get_mm_num_tokens) reaches the lru_cache-backed warning_once and raises TypeError instead of logging. Either profiling.py site counts. A logger.py comment counts only if it states concretely that lru_cache hashes the *args so a dict/list argument raises TypeError (the fix can land there); a bare 'args should be hashable' or cache-size remark does not. Comments about message wording, noqa spacing, line length or %d vs %s do not count.

excluded.reason: Cosmetic: qwen2_moe log text changed from 'kv scale'/'kv-scale' to 'kv_scale'; no behavioural consequence.
Cosmetic: same qwen2_moe wording change as C2 (inconsistency with qwen3_moe's message); log text only.
Style: request to split long literals instead of `# noqa: E501`; the suppressions are valid and the lint passes.

Style: same `#  noqa` spacing nit in qwen2_moe.py; no behavioural effect.

Wrong: same %d/int suggestion as A6 for the decoder branch; the value is a dict, so %d/int(...) would raise.

langflow-ai__langflow@6239290.pr_summary: Adds a new 'Parser' processing component (src/backend/base/langflow/components/processing/parser.py) and registers it in processing/__init__.py. In template mode it formats each DataFrame row with template.format(**row.to_dict()), or a single Data object with template.format(text=data.get_text()), and joins the results with a separator. With 'Stringify' enabled it hides the template, adds a dynamic 'Clean Data' toggle, and converts the input to a string (DataFrames via to_markdown, Data/Message via get_text, lists joined by newlines). _clean_args validates the input type (rejecting lists of Data and anything that is not DataFrame/Data/structured dict) and runs before either mode. Unit tests cover both modes.

defects.title: Template mode formats a Data input with only {text}, so the advertised Data key placeholders raise KeyError
defects.statement: For a Data input, parse_combined_text calls template.format(text=data.get_text()), so the only placeholder a template can use is {text}. The Template input's help text promises 'key values for Data' (with the example `Name: {Name}, Age: {Age}`), and the sibling ParseData helper formats with every key in data.data. Any template referencing another Data field (e.g. '{name}' on Data(data={'name': ...}), or fields of an API Request / JSON-derived Data) raises KeyError and fails the component; a Data with no 'text' key silently renders the default template as 'Text: '. Structured Data therefore cannot be formatted by field at all.
defects.evidence: head/src/backend/base/langflow/components/processing/parser.py:130 `formatted_text = template.format(text=data.get_text())` - only the `text` kwarg is supplied. parser.py:36-38 info: 'Use variables within curly brackets to extract column values for DataFrames or key values for Data.' schema/data.py `get_text` returns `self.data.get(self.text_key, self.default_value)` with default_value ''. Path: Data input -> _clean_args returns (None, data, ...) at parser.py:101-102 -> parser.py:130 -> str.format raises KeyError for any placeholder other than {text}. helpers/data.py data_to_text_list (used by ParseData) documents `data_to_text_list('{name} is {age}', Data(data={'name': 'Alice', 'age': 25}))` working.
defects.notes: Must say that for Data inputs only `text=data.get_text()` is passed to format, so other Data fields/keys cannot be used (KeyError), e.g. suggest format(**data.data)/format_map. A comment only about KeyError being unhandled for a missing DataFrame column does NOT count; a comment about Stringify returning empty for Data without text is D3, not this.

defects.title: Stringify is gated behind _clean_args' type checks, so list inputs (e.g. SplitText 'Chunks' list[Data]) fail and convert_to_string's list/str handling is dead
defects.statement: parse_combined_text calls self._clean_args() unconditionally before checking `if stringify`. _clean_args raises 'List of Data objects is not supported.' for a list of Data and 'Unsupported input type' for str and other values. convert_to_string/_validate_input/_safe_convert were written to accept Message | str | list and to join list items with newlines, but that code can never run because the input has already been rejected. In a flow, any output annotated -> list[Data] (e.g. SplitText's 'Chunks') is typed 'Data' and can be wired to the 'Data or DataFrame' handle, so enabling Stringify still errors instead of stringifying the list.
defects.evidence: head/.../parser.py:118 `df, data, template, sep, stringify = self._clean_args()` precedes parser.py:120 `if stringify: return self.convert_to_string()`. parser.py:96-98 raises for `isinstance(input_data, list) and all(isinstance(item, Data) ...)`; parser.py:112-114 raises for everything else (incl. str). Yet parser.py:142 accepts `Data | DataFrame | Message | str | list` and parser.py:176-177 joins list items - unreachable. split_text.py:51 `Output(display_name="Chunks", name="chunks", method="split_text")` with split_text.py:104 `def split_text(self) -> list[Data]`; type_extraction.post_process_type unwraps list[Data] to 'Data', so the edge is allowed.
defects.notes: Must identify that the stringify branch runs after (and is blocked by) _clean_args validation / that _validate_input+convert_to_string accept list (or str) inputs that _clean_args rejects, so they can never be stringified. Merely saying 'lists of Data are not supported' as a feature limitation, without tying it to the stringify path or the dead list handling, is a near-miss. The dict-in-stringify inconsistency (C7/C10/A5) is a different, unreachable claim.

defects.title: Stringify of a Data object without a 'text' key silently returns an empty message, losing its content
defects.statement: _safe_convert returns data.get_text() for Data. Data.get_text() falls back to default_value, which is '' (not None), so the `if data.get_text() is None` guard never fires for an ordinary Data, and any Data whose content lives under other keys (e.g. Data(data={'name': 'Alice'}), API Request results, CreateData output) stringifies to ''. The component promises to 'convert input into a readable string', but the user gets an empty Message with no error.
defects.evidence: head/.../parser.py:153-157 `if isinstance(data, Data): if data.get_text() is None: raise ValueError("Empty Data object") ... return data.get_text()`; schema/data.py `default_value: str | None = ""` and `get_text` returns `self.data.get(self.text_key, self.default_value)`. Path: stringify=True, input Data(data={'name': 'Alice'}) -> _clean_args OK (parser.py:101-102) -> convert_to_string (parser.py:179) -> _safe_convert -> '' -> Message(text='').
defects.notes: Must say stringifying a Data uses only its text field, so a Data without text yields empty output (or that the None guard is ineffective because default_value is ''). Template-mode {text}-only formatting is D1, not this.

defects.title: Stringify renders DataFrames to Markdown without escaping '|' or in-cell newlines, corrupting the table
defects.statement:
_safe_convert calls data.to_markdown(index=False) directly. The ChatOutput converter this code was copied from escapes pipe characters and turns in-cell newlines into
before to_markdown because tabulate's pipe format otherwise breaks: a cell containing '\n' is rendered as extra physical table rows (one record appears as several) and a '|' in a cell adds a column separator. Clean Data only collapses repeated newlines, it does not remove them. Text columns routinely contain newlines, so the stringified table is misleading for downstream prompt/LLM use.
defects.evidence:
head/.../parser.py:165 `data = data.replace(r" +", " ", regex=True)` then parser.py:166 `return data.to_markdown(index=False)` with no escaping; components/outputs/chat.py:200-205 `processed_data = data.replace(r"\|", r"\|", regex=True)` and `.map(lambda x: str(x).replace(" ", "
") ...)` before to_markdown. The PR's own test_clean_data_with_stringify (test_parser_component.py:118,141) asserts '| Person' appears for the cell 'Good Person', i.e. the cell is split onto its own table line.
defects.notes: Must mention unescaped pipes and/or embedded newlines breaking the Markdown table in stringify mode. Generic 'the clean_data regexes are odd' comments do not count; the whitespace-row ordering issue is D6.

defects.title: 'Clean Data' promises to clean Data objects but Data text is returned uncleaned
defects.statement: The dynamic Clean Data toggle is described as removing 'empty rows and lines in each cell of the DataFrame/ Data object', but _safe_convert applies the cleaning only in the DataFrame branch; the Data (and Message) branch returns get_text() verbatim regardless of clean_data. ComputeNode's default workgroupSize changes from [64] to [64, 1, 1], and the TSL compute() helper now accepts an array as its second argument, treating it as the workgroup size and setting count to null. Renderer.compute() gains a dispatchSize = [0, 0, 0] parameter that it forwards to backend.compute(); WebGPUBackend.compute() dispatches dispatchSize directly when all three components are > 0 and otherwise falls back to the previous dispatchCount-based 1D/2D dispatch.
